annotation.title_clean: Robot taxation as a fiscal policy instrument for sustainable employment: A scoping review with implications for developing economies
annotation.title_en: Robot taxation as a fiscal policy instrument for sustainable employment: A scoping review with implications for developing economies
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Scoping review (Arksey and O'Malley) on robot taxation as a fiscal response to automation-driven job losses and declining income tax revenue, with focus on South Africa. It argues a robot tax could offset lost revenue, fund retraining and correct tax biases favouring capital over labour.
key_provisions_or_claims: Automation reduces employment-based tax revenue and strains public finances.
Tax systems, including South Africa's, favour capital over labour.
A robot tax could offset lost income tax and fund retraining and reskilling.
Implementation challenges include defining robots, taxpayer identification, and international tax competition.
South Africa should consider robot tax measures; Korea reduced automation tax incentives.
